definition.name: Artwork Consignment Management
definition.overview:
An **Artwork Consignment Management** application operates the consignment relationship between the owner of an artwork and the party authorized to sell or exhibit it on the owner's behalf. The owner — an artist, an estate, a collector, or another dealer — is the **consignor**; the gallery, dealer, or representative holding the work is the **consignee**. Ownership stays with the consignor throughout; the consignee earns a recorded share when a work sells and must account for every work placed, sold, or returned.

The defining core is small:

```text
Consignor (retains title to the work)
└── Consignee (authorized to sell or exhibit on the owner's behalf)
    └── Specific works placed under consignment (tracked one by one)
        └── Recorded terms of the placement
            (commission/split, duration, return basis)
        └── Per-work disposition state
            (placed → on consignment → sold or returned)
```

Everything else commonly associated with these products — generated agreements, settlement statements, connected artist portals, check-in/check-out, reporting — is standard equipment in mature implementations but not what makes the category what it is.

A note on how the market packages this: in the researched sample, consignment management is almost always delivered as a module inside a gallery's operating system (on the consignee side) and inside artist studio tools (on the consignor side), with the two sides sometimes linked by connected accounts. No major standalone product dedicated solely to artwork consignment was found in reachable official sources. The structure described here is the consignment-centered core that those modules implement; see Related Application Types for the packaging boundary.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**Artwork Consignment Management**应用程序运作艺术品所有者与被授权代表所有者出售或展示该艺术品的一方之间的寄售关系。所有者——艺术家、遗产、收藏家或另一位经销商——是**consignor**；持有作品的画廊、经销商或代表是**consignee**。所有权始终保留在consignor手中；当作品售出时，consignee获得记录的份额，并必须说明每一件寄售、出售或退回的作品。

定义的核心很小：

```text
Consignor (retains title to the work)
└── Consignee (authorized to sell or exhibit on the owner's behalf)
    └── Specific works placed under consignment (tracked one by one)
        └── Recorded terms of the placement
            (commission/split, duration, return basis)
        └── Per-work disposition state
            (placed → on consignment → sold or returned)
```

与这些产品通常相关的所有其他功能——生成的协议、结算报表、连接的艺术家门户、签入/签出、报告——在成熟的实施中是标准装备，但并不是该类别的核心。

关于市场如何包装这一点的一个说明：在研究的样本中，寄售管理几乎总是作为画廊操作系统（在consignee一侧）和艺术家工作室工具（在consignor一侧）内的一个模块提供，有时通过连接账户将两侧链接起来。在可访问的官方来源中，没有找到专门用于艺术品寄售的主要独立产品。这里描述的结构是这些模块实现的以寄售为中心的核心；有关包装边界，请参见相关应用程序类型。
definition.dc:
**Consignor.** The party who owns the work and retains title until a sale. A consignor is a tracked record — usually an artist, but also an estate, a collector, or another dealer — and carries the relationship context: default consignment terms, works placed, amounts owed. The consignor is the counterparty the system ultimately accounts to.

**Consignee.** The party authorized to sell or exhibit the work. In gallery-side deployments the consignee is the operator of the system; in consignor-side deployments the consignee is an external party whose sales and returns must be recorded and, in some products, coordinated through a connected account.

**Consigned work.** Consignment is tracked per specific physical work — one record per piece, never per interchangeable stock item. The consigned item carries its attribution and identity (artist, title, medium, dimensions, edition where applicable), its imagery, its price, and its consignment state. Because works are unique, the consignment record is item-level: which exact piece, from which consignor, under which terms, currently where.

**Consignment record.** The placement itself is a managed object: a consignment list or record that binds a set of works to a consignor (incoming) or recipient (outgoing), with a title, optional start and end dates, the commercial terms, and the itemized works. The terms are the commercial substance of the record — commission percentages or splits, duration, and the conditions under which works come back. Mature implementations store default terms per consignor and allow per-work overrides.

**Disposition state.** Every consigned work moves through a tracked state:

```text
Placed / sent
  → accepted & received
  → on consignment (at a named location)
  → sold   (attributed to a specific sale)
  or returned   (recorded back to the consignor)
```

The two terminal dispositions — sold or returned — are what the whole structure exists to reach and record. A work that sells generates the consignor's share; a work that comes back re-enters the consignor's holdings.
definition.dc_zh:
**委托方。** 即作品的所有权方，在售出前保留所有权。委托方是一个可追踪的记录实体——通常为艺术家，也可能是遗产管理方、收藏家或其他经销商——并承载着关系上下文：默认寄售条款、已寄作品、应付金额。委托方是系统最终需要进行账务处理的交易对手。

**受托方。** 即被授权销售或展示作品的一方。在画廊端部署的系统中，受托方是系统的运营者；在委托方端部署的系统中，受托方则是外部实体，其销售和退货记录需要被系统记录，并在部分产品中通过关联账户进行协调。

**寄售作品。** 寄售管理以具体、独立的实物作品为单位进行追踪——每件作品单独一条记录，绝不按可互换的库存商品管理。寄售作品条目包含其归属信息与身份标识（艺术家、标题、媒介、尺寸、适用版次）、影像资料、价格以及寄售状态。由于作品具有唯一性，寄售记录是项目级别的：确切是哪件作品、来自哪位委托方、依据何种条款、当前位于何处。

**寄售记录。** 寄售行为本身是一个受管理的对象：一份寄售清单或记录，将一组作品与委托方（入库）或接收方（出库）绑定，包含标题、可选的起止日期、商业条款以及作品清单明细。这些条款构成了其商业实质。
definition.rules:
### Ownership never transfers until a sale

The consignor retains title throughout the placement. The system's records are built on this: works on consignment remain the consignor's property, appear in their holdings, and only leave them through a recorded sale or return. This is the structural difference between consignment and purchase.

### Acceptance is a recorded gate

In connected setups, an incoming consignment is a proposal until the receiving party accepts; acceptance creates the item-level records on the consignee side. Accepted consignments typically cannot simply be deleted — the placement is part of the record.

### The two sides may see the same work differently

Where consignor and consignee each keep their own records of the same work, the views deliberately diverge: the consignor's copy shows the work as "on consignment to [gallery]", the consignee's copy shows it as held stock; numbering and dates can differ per side; edits on one side do not automatically propagate to the other. Coordination of consigned-work details is partly procedural, not fully synchronized.

### Sale attribution changes the consignor's state

When a consigned work is invoiced and the sale closed, the consignor's record of that work flips to sold — attributed to the selling party — and the consignor's amount-due grows. The invoice, not the handshake, is the trigger.

### Returns are events, not reversals

A return is recorded as its own consignment-type event with its own terms and form. In some connected products the return must be recorded on the holding side and communicated, rather than automatically restoring the work in the consignor's account.

### Terms are defaults with overrides

Commission percentages, durations, and return conditions are commonly stored as defaults per consignor and applied automatically to new consignments, with per-work or per-consignment overrides. This keeps terms consistent without making them rigid.

### Status coordination is not always enforced

Some products do not block a consignor from sending a work already marked sold, or a holding party from recording events out of order; the systems track states but rely on the parties communicating about discrepancies. Consignment software records the relationship; it does not replace the trust and communication underneath it.
definition.rules_zh:
### 所有权在售出前永不转移

consignor在整个寄售期间保留所有权。系统的记录建立在此基础上：寄售作品仍然是consignor的财产，出现在他们的资产中，只有通过记录的销售或退回才离开。这是寄售与购买的结构性区别。

### 接受是一个记录的关卡

在连接设置中，传入的寄售在接收方接受之前是一个提议；接受在consignee一方创建项目级别的记录。接受的寄售通常不能简单地删除——寄售是记录的一部分。

### 双方可能对同一作品的看法不同

当consignor和consignee各自保留同一作品的记录时，视图有意不同：consignor的副本显示作品为“寄售给[画廊]”，consignee的副本显示为持有库存；编号和日期可能因方而异；一方的编辑不会自动传播到另一方。寄售作品细节的协调部分是程序性的，而不是完全同步的。

### 销售归属改变了consignor的状态

当寄售作品被开发票且销售关闭时，consignor对该作品的记录翻转为已售出——归属于销售方——并且consignor的应付金额增加。发票，而不是握手，是触发器。

### 退货是事件，而不是逆转

退货作为自己的寄售类型事件被记录，有自己的条款和形式。在一些连接产品中，退货必须在持有方被记录并传达，而不是自动恢复consignor账户中的作品。

### 条款是带有覆盖的默认值

佣金百分比、持续时间和退货条件通常作为每个的默认值存储

definition.name: Cultural Heritage Asset Management
definition.overview:
A **Cultural Heritage Asset Management** application is the registry-of-record software for cultural heritage assets: historic buildings, monuments, archaeological sites, parks and gardens, battlefields, cultural landscapes, districts, and comparable place-based heritage resources. It holds each asset as an individually identified, persistent record characterized in heritage terms — what it is, what period it belongs to, what is known about it, what protection status it carries — and anchored to a location in geographic space. Around that registry, the system captures the activities through which the heritage body understands, protects, and manages the assets: field surveys and investigations, designation and listing decisions, planning consultations, condition monitoring, and publication of the inventory to professionals and the public.

The defining core is deliberately small: a standing inventory of heritage asset records, heritage-domain characterization, and location anchoring. Everything else — interactive mapping, public web portals, consultation casework, community nomination, condition monitoring — is widely present in mature products but is an extension of the registry, not what makes the registry this Type of application.

The boundary matters as much as the definition: this Type does **not** hold objects in custody. It has no accessions, no storage locations, no loans. The moment a system must answer "which shelf is this object stored on and who may borrow it," it has become a collection-management system. Cultural heritage asset management answers a different question: "what is this place, where is it, what do we know about it, and what is its status?"
definition.overview_zh:
一款**文化遗产资产管理**应用是文化遗产资产的官方记录软件：包括历史建筑、纪念碑、考古遗址、公园和花园、战场、文化景观、历史街区，以及类似的基于地点的遗产资源。它将每个资产作为独立识别、永久记录的条目进行管理，这些条目以遗产术语进行描述——它是什么、属于哪个时期、已知哪些信息、具有何种保护状态——并锚定在地理空间中的一个位置上。围绕这个登记册，系统记录了遗产机构用于理解、保护和管理这些资产的各种活动：实地调查与勘察、指定与名录收录决定、规划咨询、状况监测，以及向专业人士和公众发布清单。

其定义性核心故意保持精简：一份由遗产资产记录组成的常设清单、遗产领域的特征描述，以及位置锚定。其他一切——交互式地图、公共网络门户、咨询案例处理、社区提名、状况监测——在成熟产品中普遍存在，但它们是对登记册的扩展，并非使该登记册成为此**类型**应用的关键。

边界与定义同样重要：此**类型**并**不**保管实物。它没有入藏记录、没有存储位置、没有借出。一旦系统需要回答“这件物品存放在哪个架子上以及谁可以借阅它”，它就变成了馆藏管理系统。文化遗产资产管理回答的是另一个问题：“这个地方是什么，它在哪里，我们对它了解多少，以及它的状态如何？”
definition.dc: The world of the application is organized around one central object and a documentation layer gathered around it.
definition.dc_zh: 应用世界围绕一个中心对象及其周围的文档层来组织。
definition.rules:
- **The record is of record.** Asset records persist and accumulate; changes are logged in audit trails, and prior states remain retrievable. Removing an asset from an official list is recorded as a decision, not an erasure.
- **Vocabulary is governed.** Characterization fields are populated from controlled terminologies so that decades of entries by different hands stay consistent and searchable. Terminology management is an administrative first-class activity, not an afterthought.
- **Spatial selection is a first-class operation.** "Everything within this area" is a core query of the Type, used constantly in casework and publishing; the map is both a working tool and an access route to records.
- **Access is tiered.** Internal, registered, and public views of the inventory differ; some recorded data is withheld from publication entirely, and unpublished or provisional entries are held for review before adoption.
- **Viewing is not consulting.** In planning-linked systems, using or reading the inventory explicitly does not substitute for the statutory consultation process; the system records casework, the legal process happens outside it.
- **Custody is absent by design.** Objects and finds appear as documentation of assets, not as accessioned holdings; the system does not model storage locations, ownership chains, or loans. This is the structural line between this Type and collection management.
- **Legacy data is a permanent concern.** Because these registries often descend from decades of paper records, bulk import, digitization, and reconciliation are standing features rather than one-time projects.
definition.rules_zh:
- **记录即权威。**资产记录持续存在并不断累积；变更记录在审计跟踪中，先前状态仍可检索。将资产从官方名录中移除被记录为一项决定，而非擦除。
- **术语受管控。**特征描述字段使用受控术语进行填充，以确保数十年间不同人员输入的内容保持一致和可检索。术语管理是一项行政上的首要活动，而非事后补充。
- **空间选择是一等操作。**“此区域内的一切”是该**类型**的核心查询，频繁用于案例处理和发布；地图既是工作工具，也是访问记录的途径。
- **访问分级。**清单的内部视图、注册用户视图和公共视图有所不同；某些记录的数据完全不对外发布，未发布或临时性条目在被采纳前会保留以供审核。
- **查看不等于咨询。**在与规划相关的系统中，使用或阅读清单并不明确替代法定咨询程序；系统记录案例，法律程序发生在其外部。
- **设计上无保管功能。**物品和出土物作为资产的文献记录出现，而非作为入藏的馆藏；系统不建模存储位置、所有权链或借出。这是区分此**类型**与馆藏管理的结构性界限。
- **历史数据是永久性问题。**由于这些登记册通常源自数十年的纸质记录，批量导入、数字化和协调对账是持续存在的功能特点，而非一次性项目。

definition.name: Digital Collection Portal
definition.overview:
A **Digital Collection Portal** is the published web surface of a collection: it presents a corpus of individually identified collection-item records — museum objects, artworks, photographs, archival material, specimens — for public discovery and viewing, through search, browse, and per-item detail pages.

It answers a specific institutional problem: an organization holds a collection whose records live in a cataloging or asset system, and it needs to put that collection in front of an outside audience — visitors, researchers, students, the general public — without exposing internal cataloging machinery. A collections management system is built for custody and description, not for public presentation; a generic website can show pages but has no item-level collection semantics. The collection portal is the publication layer between the two: it takes what the institution chooses to publish and turns it into a findable, viewable, citable collection online.

The defining core is small:

```text
Published corpus of collection-item records
└── Public discovery surface (search / browse)
    └── Per-item detail view (metadata + media where available)
        └── for an audience beyond the cataloging staff
```

Everything commonly associated with polished online collections — deep-zoom image viewers, faceted filtering, digital exhibitions, open-access downloads, APIs, multilingual interfaces — is widespread in current products but is not what makes a product a collection portal. Early hand-authored collection pages and offline-era collection catalogs satisfy the same core without any of those specifics.

The portal presents and provides discovery over the collection's records; the records themselves — their custody, cataloging, and authoritative content — live in a feeding system or, for aggregation services, in the contributing institutions' systems. That split of roles is the portal's identity: remove the public discovery surface and only the record system remains; remove the custody machinery and the portal still stands.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**数字馆藏门户**是馆藏对外发布的网络界面：它通过搜索、浏览和单个条目详情页，向公众展示一组逐一标识的馆藏项目记录——博物馆藏品、艺术品、照片、档案材料、标本——以供公众发现和查看。

它解决了一个特定的机构性问题：一个组织拥有一个馆藏，其记录存储在编目或资产管理系统中，它需要将这个馆藏呈现给外部受众——访客、研究人员、学生、公众——而不暴露内部的编目机制。馆藏管理系统是为保管和描述而构建的，而非用于公共展示；通用网站可以展示页面，但不具备项目级别的馆藏语义。馆藏门户是介于两者之间的发布层：它获取机构选择发布的内容，并将其转化为一个在线可检索、可查看、可引用的馆藏。

其定义性的核心很小：

```text
已发布的馆藏项目记录合集
└── 公共发现界面（搜索/浏览）
    └── 单个项目详情视图（元数据 + 可用媒体）
        └── 面向编目人员之外的受众
```

所有通常与成熟的在线馆藏相关联的功能——深度缩放图像查看器、分面筛选、数字展览、开放获取下载、API、多语言界面——在当前产品中很普遍，但它们并非使一个产品成为馆藏门户的决定性因素。早期手动编写的馆藏页面和离线时代的馆藏目录同样满足这一核心，而无需任何这些具体功能。

门户展示并提供对馆藏记录的发现服务；记录本身——其保管、编目和权威内容——则存在于一个馈送系统中，或者对于聚合服务而言，存在于贡献机构的系统中。这种角色划分是门户的身份标识：移除公共发现界面，则只剩下记录系统；移除保管机制，门户依然存在。
definition.dc:
**Collection-item record.** The unit of the portal. Each item is individually identified and described by metadata — title or name, creator, date, classification or type, physical description, provenance or history, rights — and commonly carries a digital surrogate: a photograph of the object, a scan of the document, a recording. Items may be single objects or compound (a photograph album with its pages, a manuscript with its leaves). The corpus may represent one institution's holdings or a corpus aggregated from many partners. The item record is what the audience finds and reads; the physical object it describes stays in the institution's custody.

**Public discovery surface.** Search and browse over the corpus, open to people without cataloging-system accounts. Keyword search across item descriptions is the common entry; browse entries — by collection, classification, creator, date, or place — give the corpus visible structure. Discovery is what makes the corpus a portal rather than a file drop.

**Per-item detail view.** Every item renders as its own addressable page: the descriptive metadata, the media in a viewer or player, the attribution and rights statement, and typically links to related items. Item pages are the portal's workhorse and its citable unit — each has a stable address the audience can link to and reference.
definition.dc_zh:
**藏品条目记录。** 门户的单元。每个条目都通过元数据进行单独标识和描述——标题或名称、创建者、日期、分类或类型、物理描述、来源或历史、权限——并且通常带有数字副本：对象的照片、文档的扫描件、录音。条目可以是单个对象或复合对象（如带有页码的照片集、带有叶的手稿）。语料库可能代表一个机构的馆藏或从多个合作伙伴聚合的语料库。条目记录是受众发现和阅读的内容；其描述的物理对象则留在机构保管中。

**公共发现界面。** 对语料库进行搜索和浏览，向没有编目系统账户的人开放。关键词搜索条目描述是常见入口；浏览条目——按馆藏、分类、创建者、日期或地点——赋予语料库可见结构。发现功能使语料库成为门户，而不是文件丢弃处。

**每条目详情视图。** 每个条目都渲染为自己的可寻址页面：描述性元数据、查看器或播放器中的媒体、归属和权限声明，以及通常链接到相关条目。条目页面是门户的主力工作单元和可引用单元——每个都有稳定的地址，受众可以链接和参考。
definition.rules:
### Publication is a controlled subset

The portal shows what the institution chose to publish — at item level and at field level. "Publish the collection" never means "publish the cataloging system wholesale." Records withheld, or fields withheld, simply do not exist on the public surface.

### The portal is not the record system

The authoritative record lives upstream. The portal reflects its feed: cataloging corrections propagate to the public view; the public audience cannot edit records. Public contributions (comments, tags, sets) attach to the published corpus as overlays without changing authoritative data.

### Rights govern delivery

Rights and attribution are displayed with the item, and they gate behavior: some items are viewable but not downloadable, some carry license terms for reuse, some are metadata-only where no image can be published. Terms of use frame the whole corpus. Access restrictions can also apply at the deployment level — some portals serve internal audiences (an intranet collection site) or restricted groups rather than the open public.

### Item pages are meant to be durable addresses

Because the audience cites, links, and teaches with item pages, their addresses are treated as stable. Redesigns and content changes are expected to preserve item-level addressing; breaking public links is avoided.

### Read-mostly by design

The defining interaction is finding and viewing. Interaction features (accounts, comments, sets, transcription) exist in many products but sit on top of a fundamentally presentational surface — a portal whose center of gravity shifts to user-generated content is drifting toward a community or social Type.
definition.rules_zh:
### 发布是一个受控的子集

门户展示的是机构选择发布的内容——在项目级别和字段级别。“发布馆藏”绝不意味着“原样发布整个编目系统”。未发布的记录，或未发布的字段，在公共界面上就根本不存在。

### 门户不是记录系统

权威记录存在于上游。门户反映其馈送源：编目更正会传播到公共视图；公众无法编辑记录。公共贡献（评论、标签、收藏集）作为叠加层附加到已发布合集上，不会更改权威数据。

### 权利决定呈现方式

权利和归属信息与项目一起展示，并决定行为：有些项目可以查看但不能下载，有些附带重用许可条款，有些仅提供元数据而无法发布图像。使用条款为整个合集设定框架。访问限制也可以应用于部署层面——一些门户服务于内部受众（内网站点）或受限群体，而非开放公众。

### 项目页面旨在拥有持久地址

因为受众会引用、链接和利用项目页面进行教学，所以它们的地址被视为稳定。改版和内容变更应保留项目级别的寻址方式；应避免破坏公共链接。

### 设计上主要是只读的

定义性的交互是查找和查看。交互功能（账户、评论、收藏集、转录）存在于许多产品中，但建立在一个本质上是呈现性的界面之上——一个重心转向用户生成内容的门户会偏向社区或社交型。

definition.name: Media Asset Management / MAM
definition.overview:
A **Media Asset Management (MAM)** application is an organization's system of record for its media corpus. It holds every piece of media as a persistent, identified **asset record** — a catalog entry bound to the actual media files (master plus proxies and other derivatives) and carrying structured metadata — and it provides the machinery to ingest media, describe it, find it, preview it, move it across storage tiers, and hand it to people, editing tools, and delivery targets.

The defining core is small:

```text
Media Asset (the record — never just the file)
└── Metadata layer carried on the record
    └── Search, browse, and preview over the whole corpus
        └── Location-aware custody and movement of the media itself
```

Remove any one part and the product stops being a MAM: without the record it is a file share or a transcoding farm; without the metadata layer it is a file browser; without corpus-wide search and preview it is an inventory spreadsheet; without custody of the media itself — tracking where masters live and moving them — it is a catalog that cannot actually manage anything.

MAMs center on heavy, in-production audiovisual media: video first, with audio, images, subtitles, and supporting documents managed alongside. They are corpus-scale (everything the organization has ever shot or licensed, not one project's bin), production-aware (media is in work, being approved, being reused), and location-aware (masters move between working storage and archive tiers while the record and its proxy stay findable).
definition.overview_zh:
一个 **媒体资产管理 (MAM)** 应用程序是组织媒体库的系统记录。它将每一段媒体作为持久的、已识别的 **资产记录** —— 一个与实际媒体文件（主文件加上代理和其他衍生文件）绑定并携带结构化元数据的目录条目 —— 并提供摄取媒体、描述、查找、预览、在存储层级间移动以及将其传递给人员、编辑工具和交付目标的机制。

定义性核心很小：

```text
媒体资产（记录——绝不仅仅是文件）
└── 记录上携带的元数据层
    └── 整个库的搜索、浏览和预览
        └── 位置感知的媒体本身保管和移动
```

移除任何一部分，该产品就不再是 MAM：没有记录，它只是一个文件共享或转码农场；没有元数据层，它只是一个文件浏览器；没有全库搜索和预览，它只是一个库存电子表格；没有媒体本身的保管——跟踪主文件位置并移动它们——它只是一个实际上无法管理任何东西的目录。

MAM 以重型、生产中的视听媒体为中心：首先是视频，音频、图像、字幕和辅助文档也随之管理。它们是库规模的（组织拍摄或授权的所有内容，而非单个项目的箱）、生产感知的（媒体正在工作中、被批准、被重用）和位置感知的（主文件在工作存储和归档层级间移动，而记录及其代理保持可查找性）。
definition.dc: The unit of record is the **asset** — a persistent catalog entry representing one piece of media. Three properties make it an asset rather than a file:
definition.dc_zh: 记录单位是**资产**——一个代表单一媒体单元的持久化的目录条目。使其成为资产而非文件的三个属性是：
definition.rules:
- **The record outlives the file's location.** Moving, archiving, or purging media never destroys the asset record; the record is what keeps the media findable and governable. Archive flows update the record with the new location and an archived status, so the catalog stays authoritative while the media sits off-tier.
- **Proxies keep the archive alive.** After a master is archived, the low-resolution proxy remains viewable and searchable. This is a deliberate design: reviewability does not depend on retrieving the master; restore is a separate, on-demand action, and restored media can land in a different location than it left.
- **Access control reaches below the asset.** Permissions commonly attach to assets, containers, and even metadata fields — different roles can see different catalogs and edit different fields — and metadata changes are auditable. In media operations the catalog itself is sensitive (unreleased material, rights exposure).
- **Status drives machinery.** Approval, archiving, and publishing are typically rule-triggered: a status change can set file movement, notifications, and packaging in motion without a human operator.
- **Metadata discipline is a functional requirement, not housekeeping.** Controlled vocabularies and picklists exist because search across millions of assets degrades quickly with free-text drift; several products make vocabulary enforcement a visible part of the logging workflow.
- **Derivatives stay linked.** Subclips, versions, and sequences reference their source assets; archiving or restoring a project is expected to handle the assets it uses.
definition.rules_zh:
- **记录比文件位置更持久。** 移动、归档或清除媒体永远不会破坏资产记录；记录是保持媒体可查找和可管理的关键。归档流程更新记录为新位置和归档状态，因此目录保持权威，而媒体处于离线层级。
- **代理让档案保持活力。** 主文件归档后，低分辨率代理仍然可查看和可搜索。这是一个刻意设计：可审阅性不依赖于检索主文件；恢复是一个单独的按需操作，恢复后的媒体可以放置到与离开时不同的位置。
- **访问控制延伸到资产以下。** 权限通常附加到资产、容器甚至元数据字段——不同角色可以看到不同目录并编辑不同字段——且元数据更改是可审计的。在媒体运营中，目录本身是敏感的（未发布材料、权利曝光）。
- **状态驱动机制。** 批准、归档和发布通常是规则触发的：状态更改可以启动文件移动、通知和打包，无需人工操作员。
- **元数据纪律是功能性要求，而非内务管理。** 受控词汇和选择列表存在是因为跨数百万资产的搜索会因自由文本漂移而快速退化；一些产品使词汇强制执行成为日志记录工作流的可见部分。
- **衍生文件保持链接。** 子片段、版本和序列引用其源资产；归档或恢复一个项目预计会处理其使用的资产。

definition.name: Museum Accession / Cataloging
definition.overview:
A **Museum Accession / Cataloging** application is the record-creating system of museum collection stewardship. It handles two connected jobs:

- **Accessioning** — the formal, recorded intake of objects into a museum's permanent collection: who the objects came from, how they were acquired (gift, purchase, bequest, transfer), the evidence that title passed to the museum, and the commitment to care for them long term. Each accessioned object receives a unique number that ties the physical object, its record, and its acquisition paperwork together.
- **Cataloging** — creating and continually enriching the authoritative record for each object: what it is, who made it and when, what it is made of, how large it is, what it looked like, where it came from, and what the museum knows about it over time.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Acquisition of objects
  → Accession (recorded intake: source, method, title evidence, permanent-collection commitment)
    → unique numbers assigned and marked on objects
      → Object catalogue record (one authoritative record per object or object group)
        → Enrichment over time (description, terminology, media, provenance, links)
```

Everything else commonly bundled with this software — configurable fields, image libraries, thesaurus vocabularies, reports, public web publishing, locations and loans — either supports these two jobs or consumes their output. Downstream custody work (movement, loans, exhibitions, conservation) operates *on* the records this system creates; the public presentation of the collection is a separate publishing surface.

A second boundary matters inside the workflow itself: not everything a museum acquires is accessioned. Objects kept as teaching props, handling specimens, or property to be disposed of are tracked as acquisitions without accessioning, because accessioning carries an ethical commitment to preserve the object for the long term.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**博物馆藏品编目/著录**应用是博物馆藏品管理的核心记录系统。它处理两项紧密相连的工作：

- **藏品编目（Accessioning）**——将物品正式、记录在案地纳入博物馆永久馆藏的流程：物品来源、获取方式（捐赠、购买、遗赠、调拨）、产权转移至博物馆的凭证，以及承诺长期妥善保管这些物品。每件经过编目的物品都会获得一个唯一编号，将实物、记录文件和获取凭证关联起来。

- **藏品著录（Cataloging）**——为每件物品创建并持续完善权威记录：它是什么、谁制作的以及何时制作、材质是什么、尺寸多大、外观如何、来源地在哪里，以及博物馆随时间推移对其了解的全部信息。

其核心结构十分精简：

```text
物品获取
  → 编目（记录入库：来源、方式、产权凭证、永久馆藏承诺）
    → 分配唯一编号并在物品上标记
      → 物品著录记录（每件物品或物品组一份权威记录）
        → 随时间推移的丰富完善（描述、术语、图像、来源、关联链接）
```

所有通常与此类软件捆绑的其他功能——可配置字段、图像库、叙词表词汇、报告、公开网站发布、存放位置与借出管理——要么支持这两项工作，要么使用其输出结果。下游的保管工作（移动、借出、展览、保护修复）基于该系统创建的记录进行操作；藏品的公开展示则是另一个独立的发布层面。

工作流程内部还有第二个重要边界：并非博物馆获得的所有物品都会被正式编目。作为教学道具、可接触标本或待处置资产保留的物品，会作为获取品进行跟踪但不进行正式编目，因为正式编目意味着承担长期保存该物品的伦理承诺。
definition.dc:
Three structures carry the whole system. Remove any one and what remains is no longer this application.

**1. The accession — a recorded, numbered intake.** Objects enter the collection through a recorded acquisition event: the source (donor, seller, estate, originating institution), the method of acquisition (gift, purchase, bequest, transfer), the date, and evidence that ownership legally transferred — a signed deed of gift, an invoice, a transfer memo. The intake that is formally accessioned is a commitment by the institution to hold and care for the objects in perpetuity, made under its collecting policy. Each accessioned object is given a unique number, and the object is physically labeled or marked with it. This number is the connective tissue of the entire system: it links the physical object to its record and to the acquisition documents behind it.

**2. The object catalogue record.** One persistent, individually identified record per object (or per defined group of objects, such as a set). It is the authoritative documentation of what the institution holds. It starts with identification — object name, classification, maker or origin, date, materials, dimensions — and is designed to grow: provenance and ownership history, associations with people and places, credit lines naming the source, images and files, and the research accumulated about the object. The record exists regardless of where the object physically is; it is the object's permanent institutional memory.

**3. The ongoing cataloging loop.** Cataloging is explicitly open-ended. Records are enriched as knowledge grows — through research, exhibitions, new attributions, contributions from communities and previous owners — and corrected when knowledge changes. The corpus is kept searchable, changes are attributable, and the accession record itself is treated as a formal register: tamper-resistant and backed up. No museum finishes cataloging; the system is built for continuous improvement, not for a final product.
definition.dc_zh:
三个结构支撑整个系统。移除任何一个，剩下的就不再是一个应用程序。

**1. 入藏——一个记录的、编号的接收。** 对象通过一个记录的获取事件进入馆藏：来源（捐赠者、卖家、遗产、起源机构）、获取方式（赠予、购买、遗赠、转让）、日期，以及所有权合法转移的证据——签署的捐赠契约、发票、转让备忘录。正式入藏的接收是机构根据其收藏政策承诺永久持有和照料对象。每个入藏对象被赋予一个唯一编号，对象被物理标记或贴上这个编号。这个编号是整个系统的连接组织：它将物理对象与其记录以及背后的获取文档连接起来。

**2. 对象目录记录。** 每个对象（或每个定义的对象组，如一套）一个持久的、单独识别的记录。它是机构所持物品的权威文档。它从识别开始——对象名称、分类、制作者或起源、日期、材料、尺寸——并设计为增长：来源和所有权历史、与人物和地点的关联、注明来源的致谢行、图像和文件，以及关于对象积累的研究。记录存在...
definition.rules:
- **Accessioning is a commitment, not a filing act.** Because accessioned objects are held in trust for the long term, what gets accessioned is governed by the institution's collecting policy; acquisitions made for other uses follow a separate, non-accessioned path. Some products distinguish the two at the record level with different record types and number series.
- **Numbers are permanent connective tissue.** Each accessioned object gets a unique number, the object is marked with it, and the number links object, record, and acquisition documentation. Numbering discipline is treated as critical: some products assign numbers automatically and refuse deviations from the configured scheme.
- **The accession record is a formal register.** It must be tamper-resistant and backed up — the institution's proof of ownership and of what it holds. Mature products support this with change history (who changed what, old and new values) and permission control over record creation and editing.
- **There is no "complete" catalogue.** Records deepen indefinitely and are corrected as knowledge changes; the system is designed for continuous enrichment rather than a finished product. Record depth itself is policy-driven — there is no single ideal record.
- **Credit and provenance travel with the object.** The source of the object (and the credit line owed) is part of the record, not an external footnote.
- **Exit is as formal as entry.** Removing an object from the collection (deaccession) is its own governed process recorded in the same system — the register must stay truthful in both directions.
- **Paper and software are equivalent in kind.** The defining records — accession register, object catalogue, title evidence — predate software and can legally be kept on paper; the software's contribution is search, scale, images, linkage, and change tracking, not a new kind of record.
definition.rules_zh:
- **编目是一种承诺，而非归档行为。**因为编目物品是长期受托保管的，哪些物品被编目取决于机构的收藏政策；为其他用途获取的物品则通过独立的、非编目的路径处理。一些产品在记录层面区分两者，使用不同的记录类型和编号序列。
- **编号是永久的连接纽带。**每件编目物品获得一个唯一编号，物品上标有该编号，并且该编号将物品、记录和获取文档链接起来。编号规范被视为至关重要：一些产品自动分配编号，并拒绝偏离已配置方案。
- **编目记录是一个正式登记簿。**它必须防篡改并有备份——这是机构所有权及持有物的法定证明。成熟的产品通过变更历史（谁在何时修改了什么、新旧值）以及对记录创建和编辑的权限控制来支持这一点。
- **没有“完整”的目录。**记录会无限期地深化，并随着知识更新而修正；该系统旨在支持持续丰富完善，而非追求一个完成品。记录的深度本身由政策驱动——不存在单一的理想记录。
- **致谢信息和来源信息随物品一同流转。**物品的来源（以及应得的致谢信息）是记录的一部分，而非外部脚注。
- **退出与进入同等正式。**将物品移出馆藏（退编）是另一个受规范约束的流程，同样记录在系统中——登记簿在入库和出库两个方向都必须保持真实准确。
- **纸质与软件在性质上是等同的。**定义性的记录——编目登记簿、物品目录、产权凭证——早于软件出现，法律上可以用纸质形式保存；软件的协作特性增强了这些记录，但并未改变它们的本质。
